why: The historical reviewed target 2.1.215 is no longer installed on this host, so the tracked run manifest and unsigned activation material packet could not be verified against a real immutable versioned file. The provider binding is re-frozen onto the CURRENTLY INSTALLED immutable versioned target.

retired_target.note: Not restored. No assumption was made about which replacement version would be current; the replacement was resolved mechanically from the launcher alias.

resolution_method: read the launcher alias ~/.local/bin/claude (a symlink, deliberately NOT bound)
resolve it to the versioned regular file it targets
confirm the target is a regular, non-symlink, executable versioned file
hash the bytes on disk twice, in separate reads, and require agreement
run the target's --version metadata probe and require it to report the bound version (no model request)
confirm device/inode/size/mtime identity is unchanged across the observation window
confirm no updater/installer process is running

observations.note: First observation of this session. The installation MOVED after this point (see below); recorded for honesty, not used as the freeze target.

installation_moved_during_this_session.assessment: ONE update, not a continuously changing installation. 2.1.220 was then stable across two independent observation windows (identical digest, inode, size and mtime; no updater running), so a stable re-freeze WAS possible. If the alias moves again before the founder signs, the manifest/packet must be regenerated and the preflight re-run: the launcher's pre-consumption provider verification fails CLOSED on drift (PROVIDER_DIGEST_MISMATCH / PROVIDER_VERSION_MISMATCH), so drift can never silently change what a signed activation executes.

frozen_binding.provider_executable_path_role: MUTABLE ALIAS — recorded for identity consistency only; never executed
frozen_binding.resolved_provider_target_role: IMMUTABLE reviewed versioned binary — this is what the spawn boundary executes

manifest_binding_change.now: sha256 of the manifest FILE bytes
manifest_binding_change.why: The production launcher (loadManifestV4) re-reads the manifest file off disk and compares that digest, so an object-serialization digest would have failed every real run closed. Binding the file bytes is also the stronger property.

builder_identity_is_separate_from_the_pr.note: The Builder's own Claude Code version is NOT the provider identity the activation binds. They are recorded separately on purpose.

no_productive_invocation.only_provider_contact: a --version metadata probe of the versioned binary, used solely to confirm the bound version
